transcript.text: I am Professor Inder Kumar Rana. I am from the Department of Mathematics. I will be taking you through a brief introduction to the course linear algebra which is going to be offered on this under the NPTEL MOOCs. Basically linear algebra has two aspects. One is static and other is dynamic. In the static aspect one studies the notion of vector spaces, the notion of a basis and so on. In the dynamic aspect of the subject one studies the concept of linear transformations. The notion of matrix is an important tool in analyzing the system of linear equations and many other concepts in linear algebra. In fact matrices help to do linear algebra on computers. So, let me give you a brief applications of the topic linear algebra. For example, partial fractions which you might have done in your school like take an example of such a fraction 2x plus 1 divided by x square into x plus 1 and you want to write it into partial fractions and you get this answer. There is a definite algorithm which works for such kind of things. Have you wondered why this algorithm works? It is because of linear algebra. More applications of linear algebra are the study of differential equations in Fourier series and Fourier analysis and functional analysis and so on. And a linear algebra also finds applications in almost all branches of sciences and engineering. For example, there is a topic called computer graphics which is a very widely used topic in computer science which involves the notion of visualizations, the notion of animation and so on. All these are possible using linear algebra. So, in this course we will study not only the theoretical aspects of linear algebra, but also we will study the applications of this topic. Basically this topic is taught at BTEC level at IIT Bombay. It is a half semester course and introducing basic linear algebra concepts to the BTEC students. They go to their respective active branches. They are able to use the concepts effectively. So, I hope you all will enjoy this course and benefit from it. Thank you very much. .
